_comment: Free-tier quotas and the endpoint allowlist, as data rather than as constants in code.
Story 3.2 AC5: these are configuration. INV-8: an endpoint absent from `endpoints` fails
configuration validation, which is what keeps a paid endpoint from ever being configured.
Story 4.7 rewrote every number below from `docs/reports/byok-provider-limits.md`, which is
a capture of the project owner's own provider dashboards rather than documentation or a
blog. Read that file before editing this one; each provider block below cites the table it
came from. Two models were removed rather than corrected -- see the google-ai-studio note.
`fallbackBackoffMs` is used only when a 429 carries no timing header at all.
`maxBackoffMs` bounds how long one call may block the Harness. A daily quota
legitimately resets hours away, and sleeping that inside complete() would hang
a Match with no diagnostic. The signal still reports the provider's true
interval, so the runner can make the long decision that is its job (AD-9).
docs/reports/byok-provider-limits.md, the Groq table. TPM is the binding
constraint on every row -- the 30 RPM ceiling is never reached by a Match.
`defaults` are the tightest published numbers on the provider (250 RPD from
`groq/compound`, 6K TPM from the 8B row) because a model with no row here is
a model nobody measured, and pacing it against the workhorse's allowance is
how a tournament burns a day's quota in an hour. Story 4.7's model discovery
makes that case ordinary rather than exceptional.
No Gemma on Groq: an earlier web search suggested `gemma2-9b-it`, the owner's
dashboard does not list it, and it is treated as gone.
`openai/gpt-oss-*` are OpenAI's open-weight models, free, with no OpenAI
account -- this is how 'add OpenAI' is satisfied at zero cost.
docs/reports/byok-provider-limits.md, the Cerebras table, captured 2026-08-01.
This block was WRONG before Story 4.7 and the correction is six-fold: it
recorded 30 RPM where the dashboard says 5, and it listed `llama3.1-8b`,
which the dashboard does not carry at all. At 5 RPM a ~60-call Match takes a
minimum of twelve minutes, which `match-feasibility.ts` computes and the
picker states before a visitor starts rather than after.
`requestsPerDay` is the one DERIVED number in this file. Cerebras publishes a
token-per-day ceiling (1M TPD) and no request-per-day figure, so 1,000 is
1M TPD divided by the ~1K tokens a Match call costs. It is recorded as a
derivation in the report's 'Derived values' section rather than presented as
a measurement.
docs/reports/byok-provider-limits.md, the Google AI Studio table, captured
2026-08-01 from the owner's AI Studio rate-limit dashboard.
`gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-2.5-pro` were REMOVED, not corrected. The
first has a 20-request DAILY cap against a ~60-call Match and can never
complete one; the second has no free quota on the measured account. Leaving
either allowlisted would keep it configurable for tournament play, where the
same arithmetic holds. The same finding is what put `match-feasibility.ts`
in the build: deleting two bad rows fixes today, and RPD / 60 fixes the
next two that go bad without anyone noticing.
The two Gemma rows are the strongest free option anywhere in the report --
30 RPM and 14,400 RPD, matching Groq's best -- and were not offered at all
before this story.
Google bakes the model into the URL path, so each model is its own
allowlist entry (INV-8), and a custom model name here needs a new entry
rather than just a different request body.
